subject: The wind's wake behind the wire as a flat isometric grid of cells, each raised cell a shed vortex roll, laid out downwind of one bright conductor on two short masts.
controls: wind: count — how many vortex rolls still stand downwind, from 2 at 0.5 m/s to 7 at 20 m/s (each roll a run of raised cells).
span: run length — the spanwise correlation: rolls go from broken runs of 2 cells to continuous runs of 8 along the wire.
gust: churn — cells are knocked off the street's lattice by 1–2 cells downwind or upwind, so the even rows break into a ragged wake.
hum: grey layer — a regular mains lattice of grey (unraised) cells fills in under the wake, 0 to ~40 cells.
risks: P15 is meant for sounds with no mechanism; pylon has one (a vibrating wire), so Gate 0's 'draw the mechanism' argues against it. The wake is real physics (Kármán street, spanwise correlation), which is why it's worth a try. It shows the wind, not the singing: the wire's modes never appear, so the note itself has nothing obvious to act on beyond a flare near the wire. Isometric cells are rhombi, not the pattern's square cells. Grid of ~104 cells plus raised faces is ~180 nodes.
